Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this call last week. Attached is Nebula's initial redline of the DPA (Nebula_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). Two quick, high-priority clarifications our team needs before we can route to procurement: 

1) Controller vs Processor — Section 1.2 currently reads that Redwood is a processor, but our taxonomy team asked for explicit language on outputs derived from customer data (specifically embeddings). Are embeddings considered "Customer Data" or "Derived Outputs"? If they are treated as Derived Outputs, can Redwood confirm whether Nebula retains ownership/control?

2) Telemetry & logs — We need a clear definition of what telemetry Redwood collects, retention windows for operational logs, and whether telemetry may contain any customer identifiers (even hashed). We also have a mandatory requirement to have an audit trail for any exfiltration investigations.

3) Execution path — Please confirm if Redwood can sign via DocuSign and who on your side will execute post-redlines.

Please see inline comments in the attached doc. Laura — looping you in as we expect legal on both sides to iterate. Rishi, would you be able to propose specific sentence-level language for the controller/processor paragraph and telemetry definition?

Best,
Samantha Jenkins

Hi Samantha,

Thanks for the redline and clear list. High level answers first, then I'll propose explicit language below.

- Role: Redwood operates as a Processor for customer-supplied data. Customer (Nebula) remains Controller. For clarity: model outputs that are deterministic transformations of Customer Data (including embeddings generated directly from Customer Data) are treated as Derived Outputs. Derived Outputs are considered customer assets in the sense that we do not assert ownership or reuse them for other customers. We can add a short sentence to the DPA to reflect that.

- Embeddings: We will treat embeddings as Derived Outputs. They are not used as training data for public models, and we do not sell or repurpose embeddings outside the customer tenancy. If you need contractual restrictions prohibiting any reuse for internal model training, we can include that clause.

- Telemetry & logs: Our telemetry is limited to operational signals necessary to run and troubleshoot the service (request IDs, latency, per-model token counts, error stacks). We segregate customer identifiers from telemetry where feasible; where identifiers are retained (for debugging or auditability) they are hashed/pseudonymized and retained for a maximum of 90 days by default. For customers with stricter needs we support configurable retention windows and can offer shorter windows in the DPA.

Below is a proposed insertion you can try in the DPA under Roles & Definitions and under Telemetry: 

--- Proposed language (editable) ---
"Controller and Processor. Customer is the Controller of Customer Data and Redwood is the Processor that processes Customer Data on Customer's behalf. "Customer Data" means any data, content, or materials provided to Redwood by Customer. "Derived Outputs" means results produced by Redwood's inference service that were generated from or based on Customer Data, including but not limited to embeddings and transformed text. Derived Outputs shall be treated as Customer Data for purposes of ownership and confidentiality; Redwood will not use Derived Outputs to train models for third parties or make Derived Outputs available to other customers without Customer's prior written consent."

"Telemetry and Operational Logs. "Telemetry" means service-level diagnostic and operational information (e.g., request IDs, latency metrics, model selection, token counts, and anonymized error traces) collected to provide, maintain, and improve the service. Telemetry shall not include Customer Content in its raw form; any Customer identifiers included in Telemetry shall be pseudonymized or hashed. Redwood retains Telemetry for a default period of 90 days unless Customer requests a different retention period in writing or via the service configuration. Redwood will provide reasonable assistance for audits and security investigations, subject to applicable law and the terms of this DPA."
--- end proposed language ---

I've attached a short doc with the clause as plain text (redwood_dpa_role_clause_v2.docx). If that fits your legal team's tone, Laura and I can incorporate the edited text into a draft to sign.

We can sign via DocuSign — please send the envelope when you are ready.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Customer Security & Privacy (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

Samantha — thanks for the thorough redline. I reviewed Rishi's proposed text and left a few targeted edits for precision in the attached DPA_redline_for_nebula.docx. Two points from Legal to highlight: 

1) Ownership phrasing — replace "Derived Outputs shall be treated as Customer Data" with "Derived Outputs shall be treated as Customer Confidential Information and Customer Property" to align with our confidentiality section.

2) Telemetry scope — please insert an explicit list in the DPA for what Redwood considers telemetry versus Customer Content. Legal prefers enumerated examples so there is less room for interpretation. I suggested retaining the 90-day default, with a carve-out that Nebula may request shorter windows in writing.

If Nebula requires (a) guaranteed deletion of trace identifiers within X days after a support incident, or (b) an SOC2+ supplement about logging and access controls, we can accommodate but will need to put those into an appendix (and those are typically billable for bespoke retention SLAs).

Rishi — once Samantha confirms she is comfortable with the wording in the attached doc, Laura/legal can prepare a DocuSign envelope. Vivek, please confirm we are OK with the 90-day baseline and the suggested audit assistance language.
